title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 51-53). Σ̃ is a compact sphere with three holes, i.e. a 'pair of pants', the basic Lego piece of the Teichmüller tower. Σ* is its interior and I = {i, j, k} indexes the boundaries. The set ε = {ω, ω'} indexes the two 'hemispheres' of the pants, cut apart by the seams joining the boundaries. On p. 51 Grothendieck defines five large simply connected open sets. Two are Σ̃_ε (ε ∈ {ω, ω'}), with 'centres' P_ε. Three are Σ̃_i (i ∈ I), with 'centres' Q_i. Using these he defines fundamental groups based at a simply connected open set rather than a point: Π_ε = π_1(Σ̃, Σ̃_ε) and Π_i = π_1(Σ̃, Σ̃_i). For any x in such an open set there is a canonical isomorphism φ_{ε,x} : Π_ε ≅ π_1(Σ̃, x), and likewise φ_{i,x}. This page begins at item 6, 'the canonical isomorphism deduced from the inclusion', i.e. φ_{ε,x} and φ_{i,x} come from x ∈ Σ̃_ε or x ∈ Σ̃_i.

Formula (30). The path c_i^ε : P_ε → Q_i defines φ_{iε} : Π_ε → Π_i, and its inverse path defines φ_{εi} : Π_i → Π_ε. The margin notes these coincide with the previous notation φ_{Q_i,ε} and φ_{P_ε,i}. In other words, the edges of a bipartite graph with vertices {P_ω, P_ω', Q_i, Q_j, Q_k} carry isomorphisms between the attached groups. This graph is K_{2,3}, drawn as a bipyramid with apices P_ε, P_ε' over the triangle Q_i, Q_j, Q_k.

Key remark. The groups are linked 'transitively' but not by a transitive system of isomorphisms. Composing the isomorphisms around closed paths of the graph gives exactly all inner automorphisms. Modern reading: the graph K_{2,3} embedded in the pants (V = 5, E = 6, rank 2) has one hole in each of its three faces. It is therefore a deformation retract of Σ*, so the holonomy map from π_1(graph) to π_1(Σ*) ≅ F_2 is an isomorphism. The monodromy of the 'local system of groups' over the graph is therefore Inn(F_2) ≅ F_2, the centre being trivial. So the family (Π_ε, Π_i) is a transitive system only modulo inner automorphisms, i.e. it defines a band (lien) / an outer-isomorphism class. This is exactly the phenomenon that later forces the use of the outer action of Galois.

Closing paragraph. The π_1 at the points P_ε, Q_i are now canonically identified with Π_ε, Π_i. It remains to 'pin down' (épingler) the π_1 at the other vertices considered so far: the boundary/seam points R_i^ω and S_i^ε, done in (31) on the next page. Then on p. 53 everything is rigidified against the standard group π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}), with its extension by S_3 × {1, complex conjugation}. Purpose: a bookkeeping/rigidification apparatus (many base points, a fundamental groupoid) for writing explicit formulas for the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the Teichmüller tower via pants decompositions.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor point: the graph as drawn shows the full triangle Q_i Q_j Q_k, but (30) only defines isomorphisms along P_ε–Q_i edges. The relevant graph is the bipartite K_{2,3}; the Q–Q segments are probably perspective lines of the bipyramid, or the hatched closed path drawn on the figure.

The claim that closed paths give *all* inner automorphisms is correct but unproved on the page. It follows because K_{2,3} with one hole per face is a spine of the three-holed sphere, so its holonomy is surjective onto π_1 ≅ F_2.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at a simply connected open subset (a 'large base point') instead of a point, with canonical isomorphisms to π_1 at any point of the subset
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid restricted to contractible base sets; precursor of tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, many base points); Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Ihara–Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids with base points adapted to the situation), in spirit

ideas.what: Isomorphisms between the base groups along the edges of a graph K_{2,3} embedded in the pants; holonomy around cycles gives exactly the inner automorphisms, so the system is transitive only modulo Inn
ideas.modern_name: local system of groups / band (lien) on a spine graph; outer fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Giraud for liens); the explicit pants-graph version appears in Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps style computations

ideas.what: Program to rigidify ('épingler') the π_1 at all chosen points of a pants piece and identify them with the standard π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller Lego / rigidified base points for the GT-action
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (Teichmüller Lego, two-level structure)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping in the base-point formalism for the Teichmüller Lego, and the inner-automorphism holonomy remark is standard. It is of historical interest as a concrete early (≥1978) explicit pants spine with five base points, but there is no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: Equation label '(B)' should read '(30)' (the previous page has (29), the next page (31)); in the text 'isom. (B)' read 'isom. (30)'.
Margin likely reads 'NB on a φ_{iε} = φ_{Q_i,ε}, φ_{εi} = φ_{P_ε,i}' (consistent with the p. 51 notation φ_{ε,x}), not φ_{Q_i,P_ε} / φ_{P_ε,Q_i}.

'Les π_1(Σ̃, base −) en les P_ε, Q_i étant canoniquement [identifiés] aux Π_ε, Π_i, il reste à "épingler" les π_1 en les autres sommets envisagés jusqu'à maintenant. Les choix naturels sont par' ('envisagés', not 'ainsi').
The figure is a bipyramid (apices P_ε top, P_ε' bottom, equator Q_i, Q_j, Q_k), not a 'double tétraèdre' with an independent hatched triangle; the hatched closed path lies on the upper faces.
